title: From Bias to Positionality: A critical grammar for Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.14079v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Bias has become a default lens for understanding what machine learning systems do and how we should relate to them. Bias is at root a deviation from a standard; in decision making systems we can supply a standard from outside: a law, a protected attribute, a benchmark, a statistical property. However, even there, biased is often used as a shorthand, without stating what the position taken is - a silent ``relative to''. In a general use of language models, nothing supplies the standard: there is no decision to audit and no counterfactual output, so the shorthand fails. We argue that positionality -- the located, articulated, owned and contestable position from which anything is said -- is the better grammar for the question these models now force: who is speaking, from where? translated_title: 从偏见到处境性：大语言模型的批判性语法
translated_abstract: 偏见已成为理解机器学习系统行为以及我们应如何与之相处的一种默认视角。偏见本质上是相对于某一标准的偏离；在决策系统中，我们可以从外部提供标准：法律、受保护属性、基准测试、统计特性。然而，即便在这些场景中，“有偏见”往往只是一种简略说法，并未说明所采取的立场是什么——一个沉默的“相对于”。在语言模型的一般使用中，没有任何东西提供标准：没有可供审计的决策，也没有反事实的输出，因此这种简略说法失效了。我们认为，处境性——即说出任何话语时所占据的、被清晰表述的、被承认的且可被质疑的位置——才是回答这些模型如今迫使我们面对的问题的更好语法：谁在说话？从何处说话？针对厂商“无处”的回答以及“处处”这一诱人的可能性，我们认为，当模型被视为“仿佛在说话”时，它就是从某个地方说话的……
tldr: 该论文提出用“处境性”取代“偏见”作为理解大语言模型的批判性框架，因为偏见需要外部标准作为参照，而在语言模型的一般使用中不存在这样的标准，因此更应追问模型“从何处说话”。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes "positionality" as a better critical grammar than "bias" for understanding large language models, arguing that since bias requires an external standard that general LLM use lacks, we should instead ask who is speaking and from where.
